2011-09-21 14.35.26.jpg.alignment_comment: The saved pose is yawed 17.8 deg toward +x, pitched 22 deg down, and its eye is 1.92 m above the shrine floor. In the photo the ledge, tier-1, tier-3 and tier-4 front edges are level to within about 2 deg. From the saved pose the model's ledge and tier-1 edges instead slope 11 and 8.5 deg down to the right (visible in the brightened render: the mirror and print frames tilt about 9 deg). The 11 photographed altar objects sit on average 127 px from their photo positions; from house.js altarCam the average is 44 px. The pillar edges lean only 0.06-0.14, which implies a pitch of about 10-14 deg, not 22. A fit to tier edges, tier ends and pillar verticals gives eye about world (-3.44, 2.7, 7.04), about 1.6 m above the floor (a normal handheld height). The direction is about (0.00, -0.24, 0.97) with roll about 0. That is about 1.0 m further +x, 0.3 m lower, about 17 deg less yaw and 8-10 deg less pitch than the saved pose, well beyond the tolerance. With the current pillar positions, no single pose fits both the pillars and the level tier edges: the best joint fit (54 px rms) keeps yaw 18 deg and leaves the ledge sloping 8 deg. So the hand yaw appears to be compensating for the pillar placement (finding 1). The camera is not inside a wall: it is in the doorway opening, 0.13 m from the jamb. altarCam at house.js:782 (eye 1.92 m above floor, 21 deg pitch) has the same too-high, too-steep assumption, and the altar objects were placed from its rays.

findings.change: Move both 'Altar pale fluted pillar' columns (with their 'Altar pillar carved capital ring' stacks) and both 'Altar niche dark side panel's about +0.3 m in x relative to the altar. Equivalently, shift the ledge, tiers and all altar objects about -0.3 m. Keep the pillar spacing of about 1.9 m. Then re-align the pose at about yaw 0, pitch 13 deg.

2011-09-21 14.57.56.jpg.alignment_comment: The given eye (-2.39, 2.17, -13.21) is not a possible camera position. The house-end-wall waterline does not match: in the render it runs almost straight down (168,168 to 139,770), but in the photo it runs diagonally from (150,215) and leaves the left edge at y about 610. That is about 150 px off at mid-frame, meaning the heading is about 3 deg too far toward +x and about 2-3 deg of roll is missing. I least-squares fitted the corner, the end-wall waterline and the far waterline with the camera fixed on the bank. Result: eye about (-1.5, 1.73, -10.2), heading about 21 deg from -z toward +x, pitch about 26 deg down, roll about -2.7 deg (horizontals rise to the right), direction about (0.322, -0.440, -0.838), all residuals 6 px or less. This conflicts with the neighbouring poses. 14.57.50, taken 6 s earlier, is posed at (9.76, 1.73, -10.03), and 14.58.02, taken 6 s later, is at (6.73, 1.73, -9.23), 8-11 m east of this one. Either one of those poses is wrong, or the house-end wall is about 9-10 m further +x than modelled. The second would make the water about 41 m long instead of 50.9 m (satellite says about 43 m). A quick look at 14.57.50 suggests its pose may itself be too far +x, so I did not list this as a geometry finding. It should be settled before the lake length is changed.

2011-09-21 15.14.02.jpg.alignment_comment: The pitch is about 9° too steep. In the photo, the corner hall's balustrade, parapet and window lines and the arcade's ridge and eave all converge at about (0.40W, 0.41H), i.e. 815 x 615 on a 2000x1500 frame. That gives a pitch of about -4.4° and a yaw of about 6° right of -x. The render's lane vanishing point sits at 0.25H, which means a pitch of -13.2°. This pushes every near object up the frame and makes the render look down into the tank-fence corner. The position is also doubtful. Eye 5.08 at x 59.14 is at the adjacent building's upper-gallery floor level (5.05); a standing photographer there would be at about 6.6. The photo's own height cues (arcade pillars against the horizon, hall columns, motorbike) give an eye about 5 m above the lane. There is a scale conflict in x. The car-to-wing-end distance ratio in the photo is about 1.55; with the model's 14.4 m gap that puts the camera at x≈41–46. But with a 48° FOV, the model's pillar and column heights put it about 15 m further back. So either this frame is wider than 48°, or along-lane spacing is about 1.35x the model's. Refit yaw and pitch from the building lines, and re-check eye height and FOV, before acting on any x position below. Lateral (z) findings use ratios that do not depend on FOV.

2011-09-21 15.19.41.jpg.alignment_comment: The given pose places pier 36.65, the gates and the rear-wall paintings (44.2, 42.35, 33.8) and doorway within about 50 px of the photo. Pitch looks about 4 deg too steep: the convergence of the capital, frieze and platform lines puts the photo horizon near y≈950/1500, not the pose's ≈1076. The eye may also be about 0.5-0.8 m too low. No pose reconciles the model's façade: a least-squares pose fit with the model's pier positions leaves about 73 px RMS with systematic height errors. Freeing the pier x positions (interior anchored) gives 25 px RMS. That fit puts the eye at about (32.0, 2.5, -8.9), yaw about 36 deg, pitch about 6 deg. The right half of the render therefore differs mainly because of geometry, not pose.
